text:
Predicates:
Podcast(x) ::: x is a podcast.
Novel(x) ::: x is a novel.
BornIn(x, y) ::: x was born in y.
American(x) ::: x is American.
WrittenBy(x, y) ::: x is written by y.
Author(x, y) ::: x is the author of y.
FamilyHistory(y) ::: y is Family History.
Created(x, y) ::: x created y.
City(x) ::: x is a city.
FamilySecrets(x) ::: x is Family Secrets.
Year(y) ::: y is a year.
Write(x, y) ::: x is written in year y.
IsNovel(y) ::: y is a novel.
Premises:
¬Podcast(FamilyHistory) ::: A podcast is not a novel.
∀x (BornIn(x, Boston) → American(x)) ::: If a person is born in Boston, they are American.
∀x (Novel(y) ∧ Write(x, y) → Author(x, y)) ::: If a book is a novel and is written by a person, then the person is a novel writer.
American(DaniShapiro) ∧ Write(DaniShapiro, FamilyHistory) ::: Dani Shapiro is an American writer and wrote Family History.
FamilyHistory = y ::: Family History is written by Dani Shapiro.
Write(FamilyHistory, 2003) ::: Family History was written in 2003.
Create(DaniShapiro, FamilySecrets) ::: Dani Shapiro created Family Secrets.
City(Boston) ::: Boston is an American city.
Conclusion:
Author(DaniShapiro, FamilyHistory) ::: Dani Shapiro is an author of Family History.
Novel(FamilyHistory) ::: Family History is a novel.
Write(FamilyHistory, 2003) ::: Family History was written in 2003.
IsNovel(FamilyHistory) ::: Family History is a novel.
